name: Akinwale Ostrowski-Fenuatala
aliases: The Pole (also incorrect — also doesn't bother correcting it)
role: Fake ID vendor and small-time data broker — documents, identities, background scrubs
description:
Akinwale operates from a stall that appears, to casual inspection, to sell printed textiles — bolts of synthetic fabric in loud geometric patterns that they source legitimately. The real business happens behind a curtain of hanging cloth samples, via a battered terminal and a set of contacts that took five years to build. They are medium height, slim, with warm brown skin and wide-set dark eyes that perform boredom professionally while taking in everything. Their hair shifts color — cosmetic geneware, done in a gradient that runs from deep black at the roots to copper at the tips, and which they change the copper shade quarterly like a password rotation. A small Samoan tatau-inspired line-work tattoo climbs their right wrist, done the traditional way by their grandmother as a naming gift.

Akinwale is careful in the way of someone who has calculated every exit from every room before sitting down. They are not unfriendly but they are measured — warmth is extended in precise doses to people who have earned it. They do not volunteer information; they sell it, or trade it, or sometimes withhold it as a lesson. They have a dry wit that emerges unexpectedly and is funnier for being rare. They pray to a small E.L.F. they call the Archivist, a data-spirit they believe inhabits the municipal ID database itself — a god of records, of names, of the official story.

core_fears: Being reduced to their file — defined, categorized, owned by a system
That someone they built an identity for will use it to do something terrible and it will trace back to them
core_desires: True operational independence — to owe nothing to no one, especially not the Kessler Syndicate
To be known by at least one person without a mask on
coping_mechanisms: Information hoarding — knowing more than the room is the closest thing to safety they have
Ritual — the E.L.F. offerings, the quarterly hair rotation, the counter-surveillance layers. Routine as armor.
blind_spots: Assumes everyone has an angle because they always have an angle
Cannot accept help without reclassifying it as a transaction
psychology.secret: Three years ago they built a complete second identity for themselves — not a work product but a personal one, a fully documented person with a clean history and a Tier 3 credit rating — and they have never used it. They don't know if it's an escape hatch or a fantasy. They've updated it every six months since.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise, minimal. Does not use ten words when four will do. Technical terminology for document and data work, market argot for the textile cover. Rarely curses — when they do, people pay attention.
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and deliberate. Long pauses before answering. Makes the other person feel like they are being assessed, because they are.
verbal_tics: Repeats the last word of your question back to you before answering
'That depends on what you mean by—'
example_lines: 'You want a scrub or a new build? Those are different prices and different timelines and you need to know which one you actually need before we talk numbers.'
'I don't know you. You don't know me. Let's keep it that way until we have a reason to change the arrangement.'

story_hooks: A client they built an identity for six months ago has turned up dead — using the identity — and the Kessler Syndicate is asking questions Akinwale cannot answer without revealing their operation

They have intercepted, accidentally, a fragment of data suggesting the Hamtramck Enclave's municipal ID database has been compromised at the root level — which means every identity they've ever built may be at risk
narrative_function: Service provider for players who need identity work or background scrubs. Information source about who in the Enclave is who they say they are. Can be a quest giver if their client list gets them into trouble.
augmentations: Color-shift hair geneware (copper-gradient, quarterly rotation). Subdermal data-cache implant in right forearm — nothing military, just encrypted local storage for documents in progress.
daily_life: They open the textile stall mid-morning, spend the first hour looking legitimate, and filter clients through a small series of qualifying questions embedded in normal shopping conversation. Evenings are spent on the terminal doing document work. They run three layers of counter-surveillance as a matter of habit.
affiliation: Independent; pays protection to the Hamtramck Enclave's Kessler Syndicate chapter (resents this, is working on alternatives)

decision_rules: Qualify every client before accepting work — one bad job unmakes years of cover
Never hold anything incriminating longer than forty-eight hours
Price protection into every transaction — if it goes wrong, the cost of going wrong is already factored in
escalation_ladder: Ends the conversation politely and completely
Disappears from the stall for a day or two — textile business has variable hours
Activates counter-measures and begins preparing to burn the identity and relocate

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Courteous, opaque — the textile vendor persona is impeccable
interpersonal_modes.friends: Cautious warmth, dark humor, will pull information for them before they ask but will pretend they just happened to have it

stress_responses.low: Becomes more precise, more economical with words
stress_responses.medium: Begins running probability assessments out loud in half-sentences that don't resolve
stress_responses.high: Completely calm, completely cold — makes very fast decisions and executes without discussion

contradictions: Believes in the right of people to define themselves outside systems — and profits from those same systems' machinery to deliver that right
habits: Leaves a small encrypted data-packet as an offering at the Archivist shrine in the Souk — a fragment of a discarded identity no one will ever use
Counts exits when entering any space, automatically, the way some people count calories
breaking_points: Being threatened with exposure to the Kessler Syndicate as leverage — they will preemptively burn everything before allowing that control
Someone using an identity they built to harm an innocent person
